pr_title: boards: m5stack_core2: Add possibility to control 5V_BUS signal
pr_body:
This commit fixes [#67277](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/67277) and hence adds possibilityto properly utilize grove extension port on M5Stack Core2 module.

5V_BUS can be enabled via regulator bus_5v. By default this regulator is disabled.
pr_comments: @kartben Do you maybe find some time to test it with some of your grove extension hardware?
@gmarull @aasinclair Could you please have a look at this PR?

issue_context.title: boards: m5stack_core2: 5V bus is not controllable
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The m5stack_core2 board features a 5v bus domain, that for example is used by the grove connector. This 5V bus is not being supplied accordingly. In addition there currently is no possibility to enable/disable this power domain.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- The external Gove connector 5V pin (2) is showing 0V.
- The documentation is not describing any behaviour on the 5V bus (https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/boards/xtensa/m5stack_core2/doc/index.html)
- device list is not showing any regulator to enable the 5V bus.
```
uart:~$ device list
devices:
- rtc@3ff48000 (READY)
- gpio@3ff44800 (READY)
- gpio@3ff44000 (READY)
- trng@3ff75144 (READY)
- uart@3ff40000 (READY)
- i2c@3ff53000 (READY)
- spi@3ff65000 (READY)
- axp192@34 (READY)
- axp192_gpio (READY)
- LDO3 (READY)
- LDO2 (READY)
- DCDC3 (READY)
- DCDC1 (READY)
- ili9342c@0 (READY)
- ft5336@38 (READY)
- lvgl_pointer (READY)
uart:~$ 
```

**Expected behavior**
The 5V may not be disabled by default, but there should be at least the possibility

**Impact**
Grove extension port is not usable properly right now.

**Logs and console output**
none


**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Toolchain Zephyr SDK 0.16.4
 - Comit SHA: 0a9728f87e41e2956cfd47de97c8f57e41b13aaa

**Additional context**
none
comments:
Main reason for this is missing support to control EXTEN pin of AXP192 PMIC.
I further investigated into this and currently prepare according fixes.

According to the schematic of M5Stack Core2 (https://m5stack.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/resource/docs/schematic/Core/CORE2_V1.0_SCH.pdf) `VBUS` is not connected to the USB-Port and therefore doesn't follow the intended usage.
`5V_BUS` can therefore be enabled independently.
To keep the PMIC in a properly defined state `VBUS` functionality should be controlled mainly by `N_VBUSEN` signal, which is pulled low  by default.

![image](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/7514817/edd6a450-a605-4f0d-b15e-477fdbf44899)


According to the official m5stack code, also the `N_VBUSEN` functionality in `VBUS` control register (REG10H[7]) is being updated (https://github.com/m5stack/M5Core2/blob/master/src/AXP192.cpp#L65-L73).
In my opinion that is not needed as VBUS will never be a valid power supply and can therefore get disabled permanently.
Fix in (67280 )[https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/67280] seems to work as intended. @kartben Do you maybe find some time to test it with some of your grove extension hardware?

review_comments: Could you return earlier if the user asks for an invalid channel?

That's not possible here. The write operation can only be executed after the switch-case above has been evaluated. The if is needed to filter the new EXT_EN gpio, that doesn't require a configuration to be written.

Is it worth moving the special case for EXTEN here instead?
It can return immediately.

I am not sure what you mean here?

Are you proposing adding a separate if for setting `*func` for the EXTEN case (5) ?
Actually I think it is fine as it is.
